claims.quote: He tucks the tin into his backpack so it doesn’t rattle.
I clip the velvet pouch with my thumb and feel the weight of the promise in my pocket, the brooch like a small, stubborn thing that wants only to be home.
He snorts and pockets the flashlight I call the Sword of Light.
"Quest supplies," I say, and unfold the map with a small ceremonial flourish. The paper is folded until the creases ache; my finger finds the village like a needle finding a thread.
I come home to find Jun on our stoop, one foot propped on the rail like he’s guarding an entrance to a kingdom.
We step off the curb together, which is our way of saying yes.

Mrs. Halloway stands, brushes dust from her skirt and turns toward the sidewalk, leaving a little line of her in the air behind her—an image I can call up any time: "A tidy blue door set on a low porch where ferns droop in green pots; the porch boards smell of lemon oil and old tea."
